assumptions.summary: Soil fertility, tree species, and forest age effects are neglected so environment and fungal characteristics dominate the model.
Pests and animal activity are excluded from matrix quality and decomposition.
Light-intensity effects on leaf structure and composition are acknowledged then excluded in favor of temperature and humidity.
Drying-wetting and freeze-thaw alternation caused by light and rainfall are omitted.
Leaching and comminution are treated as completed; only organic-matter catabolism is modeled.
Realized fungal extension is capped below the literature-based theoretical maximum.
Above a lower humidity limit, higher humidity is assumed to yield higher extension rate.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Lignin, cellulose, and hemicellulose decomposition capability is used to select six fungal types.
T_max, V_Emax, H_l, and M are retained for six named species; M is derived by Equation 6 while other columns cite literature appendices.
Fitting tuples {T, V_E, M, V_D} are said to come from source [5], but the current paper does not republish the rows.
Trichoderma, Penicillium, and Aspergillus in a tropical-rain-forest environment form the baseline for Questions 1-3.
Five named environments receive one T-H-coordinate observation-point tuple from the NCEI web map.
A different selected three-species set is assigned to each region for competitive simulation.
The single-versus-all-three comparison is repeated 1000 times to create a ratio series.

models.summary: MU-A-2021-2122025-001 (literature-derived species and regional scenario assembly): Six fungal types receive optimum temperature, theoretical extension, humidity-limit, and moisture-trade-off values; five named environments receive one temperature-humidity-coordinate tuple, and selected three-species combinations define the simulation cases. Inputs=['species_source', 'regional_source']; outputs=['species_params', 'regional_inputs', 'scenario_sets']; handoff=['species_params', 'regional_inputs', 'scenario_sets'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-002 (extension-based decomposition component): Temperature multiplies the square root of extension rate and an undetermined offset to produce a univariate decomposition component. Inputs=['T', 'V_E', 'V_D0_1']; outputs=['V_D']; handoff=['V_D'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-003 (moisture-trade-off decomposition component): Equation 2 relates log decomposition to moisture trade-off; Equation 3 exponentiates and reparameterizes the relation as lambda times a to the power M. Inputs=['M', 'alpha', 'V_D0_2', 'lambda', 'a']; outputs=['V_D']; handoff=['V_D'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-004 (additive nonlinear decomposition law): The paper adds temperature-scaled square-root extension, exponential moisture response, and an intercept to predict decomposition. Inputs=['T', 'V_E', 'M', 'lambda', 'a', 'K']; outputs=['V_D']; handoff=['V_D'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-005 (piecewise temperature-humidity extension response): A two-branch exponential response rises toward T_max and falls afterward; it is zero outside 0 to 2T_max and scales with V_Emax and humidity. Inputs=['T', 'H', 'T_max', 'V_Emax']; outputs=['V_E']; handoff=['V_E'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-006 (humidity-limit to moisture-trade-off transform): The lower humidity limit is mapped linearly to M=-2H_l+1, producing the Table 2 moisture values. Inputs=['H_l']; outputs=['M']; handoff=['M'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-007 (assembled fungal decomposition system): Equation 7 collects the combined response, parameter domain, humidity transform, and piecewise environmental extension relation. Inputs=['T', 'H', 'H_l', 'T_max', 'V_Emax', 'lambda', 'a', 'K']; outputs=['V_D']; handoff=['V_D'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-008 (nonlinear least-squares parameter objective): The paper minimizes the sum of squared residuals between observed decomposition rates and Equation 4 predictions over literature data. Inputs=['T_i', 'V_E_i', 'M_i', 'V_D_data_i', 'lambda', 'a', 'K']; outputs=['L']; handoff=['L', 'lambda', 'a', 'K'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-009 (single-sample stochastic gradient descent): A generic gradient step is expanded into lambda, a, and K updates; Table 3 cycles through N data items and returns the final iterate. Inputs=['theta', 'r', 'L', 'V_D_hat_i', 'V_D_data_i', 'M_i', 't']; outputs=['theta_next', 'lambda', 'a', 'K']; handoff=['theta_next', 'lambda', 'a', 'K'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-010 (fitted decomposition and extension calculation system): The reported fit lambda=31.90, a=1.26, K=-64.80 is substituted into the combined law and packaged with the moisture and piecewise extension transforms. Inputs=['T', 'H', 'H_l', 'T_max', 'V_Emax', 'lambda_fit', 'a_fit', 'K_fit']; outputs=['V_E', 'V_D']; handoff=['V_E', 'V_D'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-011 (continuous-rate to stochastic cellular growth interface): A sigmoid of reciprocal extension defines infection probability; uniform draws add adjacent cells, completed cells are removed, and set cardinality yields a population-change series. Inputs=['V_E_i', 'F_i_t', 'p', 'q', 'xi', 'p_D_t', 'q_D_t', 'N_D_i_t']; outputs=['F_i_t1', 'N_i_t1', 'dN_i_dt']; handoff=['F_i_t1', 'N_i_t1', 'dN_i_dt'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-012 (decomposition-rate to cell-time interface): Definition 2 divides the 122-day reference horizon by decomposition rate and grid area, then multiplies by correction factor c=5,000,000. Inputs=['V_D_i', 'c', 'grid_size', 'reference_days']; outputs=['T_D_i']; handoff=['T_D_i'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-013 (baseline multi-species cellular automaton): Equation 20 packages stochastic set growth, reciprocal-sigmoid probability, and decomposition delay; Table 4 iterates the 500-by-500 grid and reports N_i and dN_i/dt. Inputs=['F_i_t', 'p', 'q', 'p_D_t', 'q_D_t', 'xi', 'P_E_i', 'V_E_i', 'T_D_i', 'V_D_i', 'c', 'grid_size']; outputs=['F_i_t1', 'N_i', 'dN_i_dt']; handoff=['N_i', 'dN_i_dt'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-014 (occupancy-modified competitive extension probability): The reciprocal-sigmoid input divides V_Ei by a remaining-grid factor 1-sum_j|N_j|/500^2, producing P_Ci. Inputs=['V_E_i', 'N_j', 'grid_size']; outputs=['P_C_i']; handoff=['P_C_i'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-015 (competitive multi-species cellular automaton): Equation 22 replaces P_Ei with P_Ci while retaining stochastic set growth, completed-cell removal, and decomposition time. Inputs=['F_i_t', 'p', 'q', 'p_D_t', 'q_D_t', 'xi', 'P_C_i', 'V_E_i', 'N_j', 'grid_size', 'T_D_i', 'V_D_i', 'c']; outputs=['F_i_t1', 'N_i', 'dN_i_dt']; handoff=['N_i', 'dN_i_dt'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-016 (sensitivity and regional scenario decision pipeline): Figure 5 exposes the full dependency graph; Figure 6 varies T and H; Figure 7 compares each species across regions; Figure 8 compares selected competitive combinations using Table 5 inputs. Inputs=['species_params', 'regional_inputs', 'T_shift', 'H_shift']; outputs=['N_i_series', 'dominant_species', 'inferior_species', 'regional_decomposition']; handoff=['dominant_species', 'inferior_species', 'regional_decomposition'].

MU-A-2021-2122025-017 (repeated single-versus-multi-species diversity comparison): Three single-species curves and one all-three curve are compared; one thousand repeated simulations produce a multi-to-single decomposition ratio with reported mean 2.89. Inputs=['single_curve', 'multi_curve', 'repeat_index']; outputs=['ratio', 'mean_ratio']; handoff=['ratio', 'mean_ratio'].

results_trace.summary: The reported SGD iterate is lambda=31.90, a=1.26, and K=-64.80.
Without modeled competition, fungal counts rise during roughly days 5-10, decline, and are described as stabilizing around 6 x 10^4 after about day 40.
The baseline decomposition rate is reported as 0.68 after 122 days.
With competition, the late fungal count is reported around 4.5 x 10^4, 33.65 percent below baseline.
Competitive decomposition is reported as 0.39 after 122 days, 42.69 percent below baseline.
Competition is described as weak in the short run because nutrients are abundant and strong later as nutrients become scarce.
An 8 percent temperature change is said to affect final dominant-species determination; humidity changes also affect ordering.
Tropical-rain-forest inputs yield the highest displayed counts for all six individual species.
Rust fungi, Gibberella, and Fusarium are reported to fall to zero in the arid scenario.
Trichoderma is labeled dominant and Aspergillus inferior in the selected arid combination.
Aspergillus is labeled dominant and Rust fungi inferior in the selected semi-arid combination.
Aspergillus is labeled dominant and Gibberella inferior in the selected temperate combination.
Trichoderma is labeled dominant and Gibberella inferior in the arboreal narrative.
Aspergillus is labeled dominant and Penicillium inferior in the selected tropical combination.
The tropical-rain-forest combination decomposition rate is reported as 68.29 percent after 122 days.
The all-three-to-single decomposition ratio across 1000 tests has reported mean 2.89.

unresolved_questions: The six-species table says only that some parameters come from the appendix of [5]; it does not identify a source per cell, publish the source rows, state extension-rate units, distinguish measured from author-selected values, or carry uncertainty. Every downstream fit and regional simulation therefore inherits untraceable point parameters.

The notation ledger gives T a malformed temperature unit in the extracted/printed artifact, gives V_E only a numeric scope rather than a physical unit, defines G and F_i as integer sets without a biomass or mass mapping, and mixes probability, cell count, rate, and time interfaces without a dimensional ledger.

T is multiplied directly by the square root of V_E and added to an offset without a fitted coefficient or unit conversion. The claimed half-order magnitude does not close the dimensions of a 122-day decomposition fraction, and the temperature multiplier is not derived from the cited trait relation.

The log base, zero-rate handling, coefficient evidence, residuals, and observed M-versus-log(V_D) points are absent. Exponentiating and reparameterizing the asserted relation is algebraically clear, but the current paper supplies no data display or uncertainty supporting the relation it later fits.

The extension component, exponential moisture component, and intercept are added without a dimensional argument, interaction term, model-form comparison, or range constraint. The paper does not show that this additive form is preferable to alternatives or remains inside V_D in [0,1].

The response is called an Arrhenius diagram, but its exponent uses V_Emax divided by T times H rather than activation energy divided by a gas constant and absolute temperature. Extension rate, temperature, and humidity do not form an evidently dimensionless exponent, so the physical Arrhenius interpretation is unsupported.

At T=T_max the equation returns V_Emax times exp[-V_Emax/(T_max H)], not V_Emax, even though T_max is described as the optimum and V_Emax as the theoretical maximum. Figure 1 accordingly peaks well below each labeled maximum; the naming and mathematical value are not reconciled.

The exponential branches are undefined at T=0 or H=0 even though their printed domains include T=0 and H is declared on [0,1]. The separate outside-domain zero branch does not resolve these in-branch singularities, and no limiting convention is stated.

The official moisture trade-off is described as competitive ranking minus moisture niche width, yet Equation 6 replaces it with a linear transform of an ambient-humidity lower limit. No paired data, scale reconciliation, or biological calibration establishes that these two constructs are equivalent.

Equation 7 declares lambda, a, and K to be arbitrary real numbers, but a^M is not generally real for a negative a and noninteger M; Table 2 uses fractional negative M. The optimization needs at least a positivity constraint on a and a stated admissible domain.

The fitting dataset is referenced only as an appendix of [5]. The paper omits N, the actual {T,V_E,M,V_D} rows, exclusions, duplicate handling, units, and any train/validation split, so the objective and reported coefficients cannot be independently reconstructed.

Unweighted training squared error is the only fit criterion. There are no parameter bounds, regularization, identifiability analysis, multiple starts, holdout error, coefficient uncertainty, residual diagnostics, or comparison with simpler and alternative nonlinear forms.

The learning rate r, iteration budget I, sample count N, sampling order, seed, numerical precision, and stopping rule are not reported. A reader cannot reproduce the SGD path or determine whether the final iterate is stable to hyperparameters or initialization.

The pseudocode sets t=mod(k,N); with the conventional remainder this produces t=0 whenever k is divisible by N, while the displayed dataset is indexed from 1 to N. The zero-versus-one-based sample convention is not resolved.

The a update does not enforce a>0 even though later evaluations use a^M with fractional negative M. Crossing zero can make the objective or gradient non-real, and the paper supplies no reparameterization, projection, feasibility check, or gradient verification.

Only loss and lambda are plotted for one run; a and K are not shown. The loss remains highly noisy and no final loss, RMSE, R2, validation error, parameter tolerance, repeat agreement, or global-optimum evidence supports the statement that the nonlinear fit converges effectively.

One coefficient triple is transferred to every species and environment without species effects or uncertainty. The fitted response is not constrained to the declared V_D range [0,1], and the paper does not report how negative or above-one predictions are handled before conversion to decomposition time.

For positive V_E, sigmoid(1/V_E) decreases from near 1 toward 0.5 as V_E increases. This directly contradicts the prose claim that P_E increases with extension rate and means the proposed probability transform reverses the intended rate ordering.

Equation 5 explicitly returns V_E=0 outside the temperature domain, but Equation 15 then evaluates 1/V_E and is undefined. No zero-rate branch, limiting value, cap, or inactive-species rule is stated.

The set update adds a generic (p,q) after prose discusses an uninfected cell adjacent to F_i, but the equation does not encode neighborhood, eligibility, simultaneous claims, species collision priority, or update ordering. Removal timing relative to addition and grid-label updates is also incomplete.

If N_i^{t+1}=|F_i^{t+1}| is computed after Equation 17 removes fully decomposed cells, subtracting N_Di^t again double-counts removals. The expression is also called dN_i/dt although it is a discrete difference with no division by or definition of the time step.

The correction factor c=5x10^6 is asserted without derivation or calibration. Dividing a global 122-day mass-loss fraction by 500^2 makes cell time depend on arbitrary grid resolution, while cell mass, rounding, zero/negative V_D handling, and resolution invariance are absent.

The prose resets fully decomposed cells to G(p,q)=1 to simulate falling leaves, but Equation 20 only removes coordinates from F_i and contains no renewal arrival process, timing, or resource amount. This hidden nutrient input affects both late stabilization and decomposition totals.

The pseudocode performs infection work when G(p_j,q_j) is not equal to 1, even though the prose defines G=1 as uninfected and says fungi infect uninfected adjacent cells. The printed condition therefore appears reversed relative to the stated cellular semantics.

Repeated line numbers obscure nesting, and the algorithm omits random draws, collision resolution, grid boundaries, decomposition-age counters, completed-cell selection, falling-leaf renewal, regional T/H inputs, decomposition-rate accumulation, seeds, and replicate loops. It cannot reproduce Figures 3-9 end to end.

Population panels end at day 100 or 60 while the paper reports decomposition after 122 days. Exact initialization, random seed, cell-to-population scale, late-level calculation, replicate variation, and the rule producing the reported 0.68 decomposition rate are not published.

The paper discusses mutual benefit and exclusion but then treats fungal-fungal interaction as competition only, citing broad interaction literature rather than data for the selected species. This is a scenario reduction, not evidence that facilitation, metabolite exchange, or pair-specific effects can be ignored.

For a remaining factor between 0 and 1, dividing V_E by that factor makes 1/[V_E(1-occupancy)] larger, so the sigmoid P_C is larger than P_E, not lower as the prose claims. Together with Equation 15, the algebra reverses the intended competitive suppression.

N_j is already defined as a number yet appears as |N_j|; the competitor index set, exclusion of species i, simultaneous versus lagged counts, and spatial locality are unspecified. At full or overfull summed occupancy the remaining factor is zero or negative, and no domain rule is provided.

The competitive CA inherits the zero-rate singularity, occupancy-denominator failure, reversed probability direction, hidden renewal, collision ambiguity, and uncalibrated decomposition time. Replacing one probability does not by itself establish a biologically valid interaction model.

The 33.65% population reduction and 42.69% decomposition reduction are reported without a formula, exact comparison time, matched random seeds, repeated runs, confidence interval, or sensitivity to initialization. A single stochastic realization cannot support precise average-percentage language.

Short and long run are not formally defined, and the explanation relies on 100-day constructed trajectories with a hidden falling-leaf renewal process. No interaction metric, resource balance, crossover time, or independent observation validates the claimed horizon change.

The dependency graph labels the parameter data as [18], while Sections 3.1.5 and Equation 8 state that the fitting data come from [5]. Reference [18] concerns tropical litter quality rather than the trait-data appendix, so the central provenance arrow is internally inconsistent.

The four panels do not form a clean one-factor design: one panel changes both T and H, the displayed humidity shifts are not the 8% change implied by the Summary, and exact dominance times are not defined. No sensitivity coefficient, joint interaction, uncertainty band, or decision-reversal threshold is computed.

Static T-H point perturbations are used to discuss future atmospheric and seasonal change. The model includes no time-varying weather series, trend, frequency, autocorrelation, precipitation, drought duration, or climate projection, so it does not directly answer the atmospheric-trend requirement.

Each environment is represented by one temperature-humidity point with coordinates but no location name, date range, season, averaging window, measurement quality, distribution, or uncertainty. One observation cannot represent an arid, semi-arid, temperate, arboreal, or tropical-rainforest climate.

Arboreal is a vegetation/habitat descriptor rather than a climate class, yet it receives one T-H coordinate like the climate zones. The paper does not define the required arboreal environment, its tree/substrate conditions, or why the selected coordinate represents it.

The arboreal prose names Trichoderma, Hyphomycetes, and Gibberella, but Hyphomycetes is absent from Table 2 and the Figure 8 legend instead shows Trichoderma, Fusarium, and Gibberella. The simulated combination and resulting dominance claim are internally inconsistent.

Dominant, inferior, suitable, and persistent have no formal metric, evaluation horizon, threshold, tie rule, or uncertainty rule. Several curves are still rising or crossing near day 100, and different species sets across regions prevent controlled cross-region comparison.

The 68.29% decomposition rate after 122 days is not visible in Figure 8, Table 5, the pseudocode, or an equation trace from cell states. The paper explicitly omits the other regional rates for page limits, preventing reconstruction or comparison of this headline value.

The left legend names 'Only Aflatoxin', which is a toxin and not one of the selected fungal species; the intended species is ambiguous. The right panel does not say which single-species denominator is used per test, so the 1000 ratios and mean 2.89 are not reproducible.

The paper does not show that single- and three-species runs have matched initial total cells, biomass, occupied area, resource supply, random seeds, or decomposition accounting. More initial agents or opportunities could create a multi-species advantage unrelated to biodiversity.

Biodiversity is operationalized only as three selected species versus one. There is no richness gradient, evenness, functional diversity, larger community, perturbation, recovery, resilience, stability metric, field validation, or uncertainty; a noisy ratio series that sometimes approaches zero does not establish guaranteed robustness.

Terms such as accurate, precise, robust, good generalization, and high consistency are stronger than the evidence: there is no held-out prediction test or field comparison. The Article also presents broad role percentages and ecosystem claims without inline citations or clear separation between established biology and this paper's simulations.

There is no Appendix or code listing despite a nonlinear SGD fit, 500-by-500 stochastic CA, multi-species collisions, resource renewal, regional scenarios, and 1000 repeats. Data rows, hyperparameters, initialization, seeds, decomposition calculation, plots, and outputs are all missing, so none of the headline rates or ratios can be reproduced end to end.

verification.summary: The proposed extension relation reproduces the intended peak-temperature and increasing-humidity shapes; this is an internal plausibility check, not observed-error validation.
One SGD trace shows smaller noisy loss and lambda near 31.9; it does not establish global optimality, identifiability, or predictive error.
Baseline rise-decline-late behavior is compared qualitatively with cited laboratory narratives, but states, scales, and environments are not matched.
Changing only the probability interface creates an ablation-style competition comparison with reported population and decomposition reductions; matched seeds and replicate distributions are absent.
Aligned T-H panels confirm the model responds to environmental inputs and may reverse late ordering; they do not validate real atmospheric trends.
Five environment scenarios and multiple species combinations demonstrate scenario breadth, not regional predictive accuracy.
One thousand stochastic repeats expose within-model ratio variability; structural, parameter, and field uncertainty remain untested.

visualization_observations.summary: Notation ledger. Purpose: stabilize the hybrid relation-to-CA vocabulary. Encodings: symbol, definition, range or unit, and definition cross-reference. Claim: the paper separates environmental inputs, rates, sets, probabilities, and times. Construction: compact two-column table. Boundary: several units remain absent or only described as scopes.

Six-species parameter ledger. Purpose: expose the scenario traits. Encodings: rows by fungus; T_max, V_Emax, H_l, and M columns. Claim: species differ in optimum, extension ceiling, and moisture trait. Construction: literature values plus Equation 6-derived M. Boundary: provenance and uncertainty are incomplete.

Temperature-response curves. Purpose: show the two-branch optimum shape. Encodings: T on x, V_E on y, three V_Emax colors, dashed T_max. Claim: realized extension peaks at the optimum and declines afterward. Boundary: this is an equation-shape illustration, not calibration.

Humidity-response curves. Purpose: show monotone humidity response under fixed temperature. Encodings: H on x, V_E on y, three V_Emax colors. Claim: humidity increases realized extension within the proposed relation. Boundary: H is plotted to 100 while the table declares fraction [0,1], so scale interpretation must be explicit.

Unfitted composite rate-system block. Purpose: retain the entire dependency interface in one view. Encodings: decomposition equation, parameter domain, moisture transform, two environmental branches, outside-domain zero. Boundary: compact display does not resolve component calibration or units.

Nonlinear fitting objective. Purpose: show observations, prediction, unknowns, and squared residuals together. Encodings: argmin plus per-sample prediction. Boundary: sample table, weights, constraints, and holdout are absent.

SGD procedural table. Purpose: expose input, initialization, cyclic sample loop, three updates, and final iterate. Encodings: numbered pseudocode. Boundary: learning rate, iteration budget, N, seed, and stopping criterion are not instantiated.

Dual-axis optimization trace. Purpose: inspect numerical behavior. Encodings: noisy blue loss, orange lambda, iteration x-axis. Claim: loss becomes smaller and lambda approaches 31.9. Boundary: only one parameter and one run are shown.

Fitted calculation-system block. Purpose: freeze coefficients and preserve the environment-to-rate interface. Encodings: fitted decomposition plus moisture and piecewise extension equations. Boundary: no range, uncertainty, or holdout band is shown.

Extension-to-cellular interface block. Purpose: convert rate to probability, set updates, removal, and count change. Encodings: sigmoid, piecewise stochastic update, set subtraction, reported derivative. Boundary: monotonicity, neighborhood, collision, and time-step semantics need checks.
Decomposition-time interface. Purpose: map 122-day response to cell completion delay. Encodings: inverse rate, grid area, correction factor. Boundary: c and resolution scaling are not derived.

Baseline CA system. Purpose: assemble transition, random draw, extension probability, and decomposition time. Encodings: brace-delimited equations. Boundary: eligibility, neighborhood, renewal, and initialization remain partly in prose.

Baseline final spatial map. Purpose: show simultaneous three-species infection and decomposed cells. Encodings: 500-by-500 color grid and categorical legend. Boundary: final day, initial state, and stochastic variability are not in the panel.

Baseline population trajectories. Purpose: reveal early peaks, decline, and late separation. Encodings: three colored N_i lines over days. Boundary: the plot ends at day 100 while decomposition is reported at day 122.

Baseline population-change trajectories. Purpose: align phase interpretation with a change metric. Encodings: three colored dN_i/dt lines. Boundary: Equation 18 is a discrete count difference and the plotted calculation is not reproduced.

CA pseudocode. Purpose: make grid scanning and state updates inspectable. Encodings: nested time/cell loops, adjacency, probability, delay, update, and outputs. Boundary: the displayed eligibility condition and line numbering require exact implementation review.

Competition interface and composite CA. Purpose: isolate the one probability change between baseline and competition. Encodings: occupancy factor, reciprocal sigmoid, reused transition and delay. Boundary: denominator domain and index meaning are not proved.

Competitive final spatial map. Purpose: compare decomposed coverage with Figure 3. Encodings: same grid and species colors. Boundary: no matched random seed or quantitative spatial statistic is shown.

Competitive population trajectories. Purpose: support the 33.65 percent late-count comparison. Encodings: same species colors and day axis as baseline. Boundary: calculation point and replicate uncertainty are absent.

Competitive population-change trajectories. Purpose: compare early change and late near-zero behavior. Encodings: three dN_i/dt lines. Boundary: no numerical stability or stochastic confidence band is supplied.

End-to-end dependency graph. Purpose: show input, equation, derived quantity, model, and feedback handoffs. Encodings: blue input boxes, teal equation labels, yellow model boxes, arrows. Boundary: the graph labels fitting data as [18] while the fitting prose names [5].

Four-panel T-H sensitivity comparison. Purpose: test late species ordering under controlled environment changes. Encodings: aligned axes and species colors; panel titles give exact T and H. Boundary: the design is sparse and lacks uncertainty or a sensitivity index.

Six-by-five individual-environment trajectory matrix. Purpose: compare each species across five named environments. Encodings: six species panels, five consistent environment colors, common 100-day horizon. Boundary: y-axis scales differ and one point represents each environment.

Five regional competitive-combination panels. Purpose: identify scenario-specific dominant and inferior species. Encodings: one region per panel, three labeled trajectories. Boundary: combinations differ across regions, so cross-panel species effects are not controlled.

Regional input ledger. Purpose: reveal T, H, and coordinate assumptions behind Figures 7-8. Encodings: five region rows and four numeric columns. Boundary: no date range, averaging period, seasonal distribution, or uncertainty is given.

Two-panel diversity comparison. Purpose: show multi-versus-single decomposition curves and 1000 per-test ratios. Encodings: four left curves, dense right ratio series, common captions. Boundary: the legend names 'Only Aflatoxin', ratio denominators are unclear, and no distribution summary beyond mean 2.89 is shown.

weaknesses.summary: The six-species table says only that some parameters come from the appendix of [5]; it does not identify a source per cell, publish the source rows, state extension-rate units, distinguish measured from author-selected values, or carry uncertainty. Every downstream fit and regional simulation therefore inherits untraceable point parameters.

The notation ledger gives T a malformed temperature unit in the extracted/printed artifact, gives V_E only a numeric scope rather than a physical unit, defines G and F_i as integer sets without a biomass or mass mapping, and mixes probability, cell count, rate, and time interfaces without a dimensional ledger.

T is multiplied directly by the square root of V_E and added to an offset without a fitted coefficient or unit conversion. The claimed half-order magnitude does not close the dimensions of a 122-day decomposition fraction, and the temperature multiplier is not derived from the cited trait relation.

The log base, zero-rate handling, coefficient evidence, residuals, and observed M-versus-log(V_D) points are absent. Exponentiating and reparameterizing the asserted relation is algebraically clear, but the current paper supplies no data display or uncertainty supporting the relation it later fits.

The extension component, exponential moisture component, and intercept are added without a dimensional argument, interaction term, model-form comparison, or range constraint. The paper does not show that this additive form is preferable to alternatives or remains inside V_D in [0,1].

The response is called an Arrhenius diagram, but its exponent uses V_Emax divided by T times H rather than activation energy divided by a gas constant and absolute temperature. Extension rate, temperature, and humidity do not form an evidently dimensionless exponent, so the physical Arrhenius interpretation is unsupported.

At T=T_max the equation returns V_Emax times exp[-V_Emax/(T_max H)], not V_Emax, even though T_max is described as the optimum and V_Emax as the theoretical maximum. Figure 1 accordingly peaks well below each labeled maximum; the naming and mathematical value are not reconciled.

The exponential branches are undefined at T=0 or H=0 even though their printed domains include T=0 and H is declared on [0,1]. The separate outside-domain zero branch does not resolve these in-branch singularities, and no limiting convention is stated.

The official moisture trade-off is described as competitive ranking minus moisture niche width, yet Equation 6 replaces it with a linear transform of an ambient-humidity lower limit. No paired data, scale reconciliation, or biological calibration establishes that these two constructs are equivalent.

Equation 7 declares lambda, a, and K to be arbitrary real numbers, but a^M is not generally real for a negative a and noninteger M; Table 2 uses fractional negative M. The optimization needs at least a positivity constraint on a and a stated admissible domain.

The fitting dataset is referenced only as an appendix of [5]. The paper omits N, the actual {T,V_E,M,V_D} rows, exclusions, duplicate handling, units, and any train/validation split, so the objective and reported coefficients cannot be independently reconstructed.

Unweighted training squared error is the only fit criterion. There are no parameter bounds, regularization, identifiability analysis, multiple starts, holdout error, coefficient uncertainty, residual diagnostics, or comparison with simpler and alternative nonlinear forms.

The learning rate r, iteration budget I, sample count N, sampling order, seed, numerical precision, and stopping rule are not reported. A reader cannot reproduce the SGD path or determine whether the final iterate is stable to hyperparameters or initialization.

The pseudocode sets t=mod(k,N); with the conventional remainder this produces t=0 whenever k is divisible by N, while the displayed dataset is indexed from 1 to N. The zero-versus-one-based sample convention is not resolved.

The a update does not enforce a>0 even though later evaluations use a^M with fractional negative M. Crossing zero can make the objective or gradient non-real, and the paper supplies no reparameterization, projection, feasibility check, or gradient verification.

Only loss and lambda are plotted for one run; a and K are not shown. The loss remains highly noisy and no final loss, RMSE, R2, validation error, parameter tolerance, repeat agreement, or global-optimum evidence supports the statement that the nonlinear fit converges effectively.

One coefficient triple is transferred to every species and environment without species effects or uncertainty. The fitted response is not constrained to the declared V_D range [0,1], and the paper does not report how negative or above-one predictions are handled before conversion to decomposition time.

For positive V_E, sigmoid(1/V_E) decreases from near 1 toward 0.5 as V_E increases. This directly contradicts the prose claim that P_E increases with extension rate and means the proposed probability transform reverses the intended rate ordering.

Equation 5 explicitly returns V_E=0 outside the temperature domain, but Equation 15 then evaluates 1/V_E and is undefined. No zero-rate branch, limiting value, cap, or inactive-species rule is stated.

The set update adds a generic (p,q) after prose discusses an uninfected cell adjacent to F_i, but the equation does not encode neighborhood, eligibility, simultaneous claims, species collision priority, or update ordering. Removal timing relative to addition and grid-label updates is also incomplete.

If N_i^{t+1}=|F_i^{t+1}| is computed after Equation 17 removes fully decomposed cells, subtracting N_Di^t again double-counts removals. The expression is also called dN_i/dt although it is a discrete difference with no division by or definition of the time step.

The correction factor c=5x10^6 is asserted without derivation or calibration. Dividing a global 122-day mass-loss fraction by 500^2 makes cell time depend on arbitrary grid resolution, while cell mass, rounding, zero/negative V_D handling, and resolution invariance are absent.

The prose resets fully decomposed cells to G(p,q)=1 to simulate falling leaves, but Equation 20 only removes coordinates from F_i and contains no renewal arrival process, timing, or resource amount. This hidden nutrient input affects both late stabilization and decomposition totals.

The pseudocode performs infection work when G(p_j,q_j) is not equal to 1, even though the prose defines G=1 as uninfected and says fungi infect uninfected adjacent cells. The printed condition therefore appears reversed relative to the stated cellular semantics.

Repeated line numbers obscure nesting, and the algorithm omits random draws, collision resolution, grid boundaries, decomposition-age counters, completed-cell selection, falling-leaf renewal, regional T/H inputs, decomposition-rate accumulation, seeds, and replicate loops. It cannot reproduce Figures 3-9 end to end.

Population panels end at day 100 or 60 while the paper reports decomposition after 122 days. Exact initialization, random seed, cell-to-population scale, late-level calculation, replicate variation, and the rule producing the reported 0.68 decomposition rate are not published.

The paper discusses mutual benefit and exclusion but then treats fungal-fungal interaction as competition only, citing broad interaction literature rather than data for the selected species. This is a scenario reduction, not evidence that facilitation, metabolite exchange, or pair-specific effects can be ignored.

For a remaining factor between 0 and 1, dividing V_E by that factor makes 1/[V_E(1-occupancy)] larger, so the sigmoid P_C is larger than P_E, not lower as the prose claims. Together with Equation 15, the algebra reverses the intended competitive suppression.

N_j is already defined as a number yet appears as |N_j|; the competitor index set, exclusion of species i, simultaneous versus lagged counts, and spatial locality are unspecified. At full or overfull summed occupancy the remaining factor is zero or negative, and no domain rule is provided.

The competitive CA inherits the zero-rate singularity, occupancy-denominator failure, reversed probability direction, hidden renewal, collision ambiguity, and uncalibrated decomposition time. Replacing one probability does not by itself establish a biologically valid interaction model.

The 33.65% population reduction and 42.69% decomposition reduction are reported without a formula, exact comparison time, matched random seeds, repeated runs, confidence interval, or sensitivity to initialization. A single stochastic realization cannot support precise average-percentage language.

Short and long run are not formally defined, and the explanation relies on 100-day constructed trajectories with a hidden falling-leaf renewal process. No interaction metric, resource balance, crossover time, or independent observation validates the claimed horizon change.

The dependency graph labels the parameter data as [18], while Sections 3.1.5 and Equation 8 state that the fitting data come from [5]. Reference [18] concerns tropical litter quality rather than the trait-data appendix, so the central provenance arrow is internally inconsistent.

The four panels do not form a clean one-factor design: one panel changes both T and H, the displayed humidity shifts are not the 8% change implied by the Summary, and exact dominance times are not defined. No sensitivity coefficient, joint interaction, uncertainty band, or decision-reversal threshold is computed.

Static T-H point perturbations are used to discuss future atmospheric and seasonal change. The model includes no time-varying weather series, trend, frequency, autocorrelation, precipitation, drought duration, or climate projection, so it does not directly answer the atmospheric-trend requirement.

Each environment is represented by one temperature-humidity point with coordinates but no location name, date range, season, averaging window, measurement quality, distribution, or uncertainty. One observation cannot represent an arid, semi-arid, temperate, arboreal, or tropical-rainforest climate.

Arboreal is a vegetation/habitat descriptor rather than a climate class, yet it receives one T-H coordinate like the climate zones. The paper does not define the required arboreal environment, its tree/substrate conditions, or why the selected coordinate represents it.

The arboreal prose names Trichoderma, Hyphomycetes, and Gibberella, but Hyphomycetes is absent from Table 2 and the Figure 8 legend instead shows Trichoderma, Fusarium, and Gibberella. The simulated combination and resulting dominance claim are internally inconsistent.

Dominant, inferior, suitable, and persistent have no formal metric, evaluation horizon, threshold, tie rule, or uncertainty rule. Several curves are still rising or crossing near day 100, and different species sets across regions prevent controlled cross-region comparison.

The 68.29% decomposition rate after 122 days is not visible in Figure 8, Table 5, the pseudocode, or an equation trace from cell states. The paper explicitly omits the other regional rates for page limits, preventing reconstruction or comparison of this headline value.

The left legend names 'Only Aflatoxin', which is a toxin and not one of the selected fungal species; the intended species is ambiguous. The right panel does not say which single-species denominator is used per test, so the 1000 ratios and mean 2.89 are not reproducible.

The paper does not show that single- and three-species runs have matched initial total cells, biomass, occupied area, resource supply, random seeds, or decomposition accounting. More initial agents or opportunities could create a multi-species advantage unrelated to biodiversity.

Biodiversity is operationalized only as three selected species versus one. There is no richness gradient, evenness, functional diversity, larger community, perturbation, recovery, resilience, stability metric, field validation, or uncertainty; a noisy ratio series that sometimes approaches zero does not establish guaranteed robustness.

Terms such as accurate, precise, robust, good generalization, and high consistency are stronger than the evidence: there is no held-out prediction test or field comparison. The Article also presents broad role percentages and ecosystem claims without inline citations or clear separation between established biology and this paper's simulations.

writing_logic.summary: input: the official decomposition, interaction, environment, region, diversity, and communication deliverables | rhetorical job: compress the paper into six visual paragraphs that retain methods, horizons, baselines, and headline quantities | analytical job: summarize the relation-fit-to-cellular-simulation chain plus competition, sensitivity, regional, and diversity comparisons | output: a condition-aware model-and-result map with 0.68, 0.39, 33.65%, 42.69%, 68.29%, and 2.89 anchored to their scenarios | handoff: Introduction expands the system stakes, task wording, evidence base, and execution route

input: forest material cycling, fungal mechanism literature, and the official task | rhetorical job: move from system context through evidence to an explicit work portfolio and section route | analytical job: select extension, moisture, temperature, cellular state, interaction, and scenario variables | output: a literature-supported data-model-simulation roadmap | handoff: Problem Restatement preserves each required output before assumptions narrow the scope

input: the official Problem A wording and fungal spatial capability | rhetorical job: translate six deliverables into distinct modeling, horizon, region, diversity, and audience obligations | analytical job: retain multi-species decomposition, interaction, rapid variation, trend, persistence, and community-efficiency requirements | output: a complete requirement ledger | handoff: Assumptions declares which biological and environmental mechanisms the solution will omit

input: broad forest drivers, decomposition stages, theoretical extension, and humidity thresholds | rhetorical job: pair seven scope reductions with immediate reasons or sources | analytical job: exclude soil/tree/age, animals, light, cyclic physical processes, and early decomposition stages while retaining T, H, traits, and catabolism | output: a bounded modeling domain and monotonic/cap constraints | handoff: Notation gives every retained state, trait, probability, and time a stable symbol

input: the variables created by the assumptions and planned model chain | rhetorical job: provide a symbol-definition-range ledger before the equations | analytical job: distinguish extension, decomposition, moisture, grid state, species sets, probabilities, and completion time | output: Table 1 with reusable subscript and set conventions | handoff: Data Preprocessing resolves the species and region parameters

input: literature trait values, humidity limits, weather points, and selected species combinations | rhetorical job: make the scenario inputs visible before simulation | analytical job: assemble six species, five T-H-coordinate points, a tropical baseline trio, regional trios, and 1000 stochastic repeats | output: typed species, regional, and scenario input tables | handoff: Model Establishment converts these inputs into extension and decomposition responses
